notes:
Summary: Octant Dynamics is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for doc-search + customer chat routing across global DCs. Primary drivers: strict latency SLOs for SLA-bound customers, cost predictability, and on-prem/VPC placement for shipment PII. They run heavy batch embedding pipelines for route-optimization models during nightly windows and a live chat product for carriers during business hours.

Key excerpts from calls: 
- 'We need 95th <200ms for chat at steady-state, 99th <400ms during short bursts' — CTO (2025-02-18).
- Procurement: wants a single-line SOW with clear outage remedies; legal requests retention & data residency language.

Dedicated sizing workshop outputs (workshop 2025-02-25): 
- Measured baseline traffic (pilot): 12 QPS average for support chat, but internal forecasts expect 60 QPS steady-state once expanded to EU region.
- Average request size: ~250 tokens (prompt+response); embedding jobs vary (5k-50k tokens per batch).
- Steady-state compute need: 60 QPS * 250 tokens = 15,000 tokens/sec sustained.
- Peak planning: marketing + morning batch overlap could push to 500 QPS burst (peak tokens/sec ~125,000).
- Latency target: 95th <= 200ms for chat generation; throughput SLA at 99% of minutes not to drop below 70% of provisioned QPS.

Recommended Redwood Dedicated configuration (prelim): 
- Reserved pool: 12 x A100-style GPUs (mix of high-memory and one-shot low-latency nodes) with autoscale buffer of 3 spare GPUs for burst. Rationale: model is a quantized Llama-3 variant; inference perf ~1.2k tokens/sec/GPU under target latency with batching. 12 GPUs -> ~14.4k tokens/sec baseline, supplemented by batching and prefix caching to hit steady-state 15k tokens/sec. Use burstable capacity + routing to hosted fallback for spikes.
- Batching strategy: 25–40ms bundling windows, dynamic batching based on queue length to preserve 95th latency.
- KV/prefix caching: enable cross-request prefix caching for repeated prompts (carrier templates) to cut token work by ~18% in production.
- Quantization: recommend int8 inference for non-LLR layers to reduce memory and increase throughput; verify QA in POC.

SLA & commercial notes: 
- Octant expects 99.95% uptime for critical production flows; Redwood default 99.9% with credit tiers. AE action: propose custom SLA addendum with graded credits (99.9->credit small, 99.5->larger, <99% -> termination rights after cure).
- Maintenance windows: Octant requires not more than 4 scheduled maintenance outages/year impacting EU region.

POC plan & Acceptance Criteria: 
- POC length: 6 weeks (2-week deploy + 3-week ramp + 1-week soak).
- Success metrics: sustain 60 QPS steady-state with 95th latency <200ms for 30 consecutive days in soak; embedding batch throughput targets (X Batches/hour); cost per 1M tokens within 12% of Redwood optimize projection.
- Data/security: SSO via SAML configured; KMS integration for keys; audit_log streaming to Octant SIEM.
